clue.text: In which one may pick apples or a variety of beet?

definitions.text: In which one may pick apples

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leaf beet, a variety of the beet plant

explanation.surface: A riddle asking where apples, or perhaps beetroot, get picked.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees where apples are grown and gathered.

clue.text: In agreement with forward on team

parts.note: on means forward, as in 'move on'
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A player in step with the forwards in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To be onside is to be supportive, in agreement with someone's plans.

clue.text: Bread from dining room brought over after tea

indicators.note: after places the reversed room following the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: brought over suggests the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a hall is a college or institutional dining room

explanation.surface: Bread carried out of the dining room once tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Hall here is the college dining hall; cha is old slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Challah is a braided Jewish loaf eaten on the Sabbath, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Valued a piano, much admired

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
praised means much admired

explanation.surface: Someone valued a piano that everyone admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Appraised means assessed for worth, so valued in the sense of priced.

clue.text: Betray twin on trial

parts.note: a double is a twin, an exact likeness
a cross is a trial or burden, as in a cross to bear

explanation.surface: Someone betrays their twin who is on trial in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to cheat or betray an ally.

clue.text: Who killed Cock Robin using extremely sharp weapon?

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters of the next word, its first and last

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme question of who killed Cock Robin, and with what sharp weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the sparrow confesses: 'I, said the Sparrow, with my bow and arrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional rhyme the bird that killed Cock Robin is the sparrow.

clue.text: Spot or mole?

definitions.meaning: to spot is to catch sight of
a mole is a secret agent planted inside an organisation

explanation.definitionFit: To spy is to spot something, and a spy is a mole working in secret.

clue.text: Horrify a European after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means the word has been turned round

parts.note: a Lapp is a European from Lapland

explanation.surface: Something horrifies a European after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' tempts as a political uprising, but it only means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill someone with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Full? Ordered peer allowed in!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
ordered means arranged, so the letters of peer are put in a new order

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A doorman told to let a peer into a full venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially well fed.

clue.text: Circumspect about river worker giving guarantee

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: wary means circumspect, cautious
an ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A cautious river worker hands over a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, so the phrase giving guarantee stands for it here.

clue.text: Mark's job in tax

parts.note: a stamp is a mark impressed on something
a duty is a job or task

explanation.surface: Mark works in the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp duty is a British tax charged on property purchases and documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp duty is a tax levied on legal documents and house sales.

clue.text: Short essay produced by pair about primate

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A short essay written by two people about a primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a short essay or dissertation, as read to a learned society.

clue.text: Girl's article on small food shop

indicators.note: in an across clue on puts the article after the shop

parts.note: a deli is a small delicatessen
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl writing an article about a local delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a girl's name, as in the cook Delia Smith.

clue.text: Saintly child from Stowe accepting pounds to levitate mysteriously

indicators.note: accepting means the anagram takes the extra letter inside it
mysteriously suggests the letters of levitate are mixed up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A saintly child seen levitating mysteriously after taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' rearranges LEVITATE as LITTEEVA; 'accepting' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Eva is the angelic child in Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel Uncle Tom's Cabin.

clue.text: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?

definitions.text: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?

parts.words: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?
parts.note: the plane seems an aircraft needing an engineer, but it is the plane tree, needing a specialist in tree care

explanation.definitionFit: An arboriculturist who treats diseased or damaged trees, such as a plane.

clue.text: The Bond novel?

parts.note: a novel about James Bond would be about a spy; the title meant is Joseph Conrad's novel of a spy

explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's spy novel takes its title from the profession James Bond follows.

clue.text: Dancing to it, again causing disquiet

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancing to the same tune again is upsetting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of anxiety or nervous disquiet.

clue.text: Film star, no sailor, on tug on holiday

indicators.note: no means the sailor is taken out of the star

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to tow is to tug
away means on holiday

explanation.surface: A film star who is no sailor ends up aboard a tug for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes TAR from STAR, leaving S. Stowaway is a 1936 Shirley Temple film.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowaway is the title of a 1936 film starring Shirley Temple.

clue.text: Drop rest on creepy-crawly

parts.note: a trapdoor is a drop, as on a gallows
a spider is a cue rest with raised legs, used in snooker

explanation.surface: Someone lets a creepy-crawly fall onto a piece of resting gear.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a spider is a rest with an arched head that lifts the cue over balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapdoor spider is a burrowing spider, a creepy-crawly that hides under a hinged lid.

clue.text: Former social worker without equal, covering miles on runs

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps round the letter

parts.note: alone means unique, without equal
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A peerless former social worker covering miles on runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a hospital social worker, a role since renamed.

clue.text: Ask earnestly to go in and dine, being short of energy

indicators.note: being short of means a letter is removed

parts.note: to enter is to go in
to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: Someone begs a tired friend to come in and eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short of' removes an E from ENTEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead or beg earnestly.

clue.text: Stop talking in jail

definitions.meaning: a curt order to be quiet

explanation.definitionFit: Shut up is both a rude order for silence and a phrase meaning imprisoned.

clue.text: A rake might be more prudent around sandy desert state

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the second

parts.note: wiser means more prudent
Oman is an Arabian state of largely sandy desert

explanation.surface: A rake might be wiser than to go wandering around a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool, but it is the old word for a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man who chases women, a philanderer.

clue.text: Girl Irish boy stood up

indicators.note: stood up means the word is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Aidan is an Irish boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl was stood up by her Irish boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a girl's name, as in the gymnast Nadia Comaneci.

clue.text: I may go after this character

definitions.text: I may go after this character

parts.words: I may go after this character
parts.note: it reads as a pursuit, but it is about alphabetical order: the letter I comes after the letter named

explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the name of the letter H, which comes just before I in the alphabet.

clue.text: Pasty leading journalist declined

parts.note: pasty means pale, wan
ED is short for editor, the leading journalist

explanation.surface: A pale chief journalist turned down the offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to decline or diminish, as the moon does.

clue.text: Quiet, living in a place such as Cleveland?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a resident is living in a place

explanation.surface: A quiet resident of some town such as Cleveland, Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleveland' looks like the Ohio city, but it is Grover Cleveland, US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was twice President of the United States, an example of the office.

clue.text: Name of writer, somewhat onomatopoeic

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A writer whose name is a bit onomatopoeic.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer of tales and poems.

clue.text: What a caddy should know: for example, a cart that needs pulling round

indicators.note: pulling round means the whole run is turned back to front

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: Golf trivia: a caddy's trolley that must be hauled round the course.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray is a low heavy cart; the reversal runs over the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the yardage is the distance to the hole, which a caddy must judge.

clue.text: No end to Coronation Street, soap shown regularly without a break

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end to means the last letter of the next word
shown regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Coronation Street is on air continuously, a soap that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstop means continuing without any pause or break.
